title: GENPLAT: an Automated Platform for Biomass Enzyme Discovery and Cocktail Optimization
protocol: Produce proteins in Pichia pastoris by cloning genes into vectors pPICZ or pPICZα and transforming them into P. pastoris.
Grow cells in 300-ml batches in baffled 500-ml flasks with methanol induction every 24 hours.
Concentrate and desalt the culture filtrates by tangential flow filtration.
Store enzymes in small aliquots in 20% glycerol at -80°C.
Input the number of enzymes, their proportions, and type of experimental design into Design-Expert software.
Calculate enzyme amounts to achieve a total loading of 15 mg/g glucan.
Generate Excel worksheets specifying source labware, source wells, destination labware, destination wells, and transfer volumes for dispensing water and enzymes.
Import the generated Excel worksheets into Biomek FXP software using the transfer-from-file function.
Suspend biomass slurry in 50 mM sodium citrate, pH 4.8, containing tetracycline and cycloheximide at 5 μg/ml each.
Robotically pipette 200 μl of the slurry into each well of a 96-well deep-well reaction plate using Span-8 1000-μl pipet tips with the last 0.5 cm cut off.
Mix the slurry once at 100 μl/sec and then aspirate the same volume from the paddle reservoir and dispense into the plates.
Dispense enzymes into the same plate using the program entered into the Beckman FX.
Seal the plates with pierceable capmats.
Invert and tap the plates several times to overcome surface tension.
Place the plates at 50°C for 48 hr in the hybridization incubator rotating at 10 rpm.
Centrifuge the reaction plates for 3 min at 1250 x g in a swinging bucket centrifuge.
Transfer 100 μl of the supernatant into regular 96-well plates using the AP96 pod of the Biomek FX.
Incubate the plates at 90-95°C for 10 min to inactivate the enzymes, and then centrifuge at 1250 x g for 30 sec.
Transfer 12 μl of the supernatants into regular 96-well plates for Glc measurements.
Add 192 μl of glucose oxidase/peroxidase (GOPOD) reagent to each well.
Incubate the plates at 50°C for 20 min and read absorbances at 510 nm in a microplate reader using blank reaction mixture with no enzyme.
Transfer 4 μl of supernatant into 384-well plates for Xyl measurements.
Add assay reagents to each well.
Read the plates at 340 nm using blank reaction mixture with no enzyme.
Convert absorbance values to their % Glc and Xyl yields based on known content.
Import these percentages as responses into Design-Expert software.
Check statistical parameters to ensure criteria for a robust model are fulfilled.
Confirm the best model prediction experimentally.
